title: How to Start Medical Research | MEDX Research Compass
description: A step-by-step research roadmap for medical and health-science students: find a question, review the literature, design a study, handle ethics, analyse data, and publish.

faq.question: Do I need previous research experience to start?
faq.answer: No. Most students begin with literature searches, data checking, recruitment support, or ethics documentation. The important things are supervision, reliability, and a clear understanding of your role.

faq.question: How long does a first research project take?
faq.answer: It depends on the design. A secondary analysis or review may take a few months; a prospective study with recruitment and follow-up can take much longer. Plan backwards from your deadline and choose a feasible scope.

faq.question: Can I publish without a lab?
faq.answer: Yes. Systematic reviews, secondary analyses, case reports, qualitative work, and health services research can be done without a bench lab. You still need mentorship, ethics review where required, and a credible reporting plan.

faq.question: What should I do first?
faq.answer: Choose one focused question, read recent literature, and speak to a mentor about a small, realistic contribution. Use the six-step Research Compass to decide what to do next.

title: What is Clinical Research? Definition & Methods (2026)
description: Clinical research explained: definition, types, phases and methods. Free guide by MedX R&ED for students entering global health research.

faq.question: Do I need a medical degree to take part in clinical research?
faq.answer: No. Clinical research teams include statisticians, data managers, nurses, public health specialists, and students from many backgrounds. Medical and health-science students often start with literature review, data collection, or study coordination. What matters most is training, supervision, and a clear understanding of ethics and methods.

faq.question: Is clinical research the same as a clinical trial?
faq.answer: No. A clinical trial is one type of clinical research, usually an interventional study that tests a treatment or prevention strategy. Clinical research also includes observational studies, diagnostic accuracy studies, qualitative work, and health services research.

faq.question: How long does a clinical research project take?
faq.answer: It depends on the question. A secondary analysis of existing data may take months, while a prospective trial can take years. Ethics approval, recruitment, and follow-up often take longer than students expect, so plan backwards from your deadlines and choose a feasible scope.

faq.question: What should I learn first?
faq.answer: Start with study design, basic biostatistics, critical appraisal, and research ethics. These four areas help you read papers intelligently and avoid common mistakes. Practical experience with a mentor is the best complement to structured learning.
